page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The configuration provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB per core, and includes 2835 GB of bundled local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng, as well as Passmark CPU and memory tests. It exhibits strong performance in cryptographic operations, database tasks, and Redis SET operations, which reach 63.99 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth for cached small-block reads is highly efficient at 3648.63 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write speeds drop to average levels.

While the server excels at processing small language models, achieving 2976.52 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a 135M model, it experiences a significant performance degradation on larger models, dropping to a poor 2.52 tokens/sec for text generation on a 70B model. This indicates a clear tradeoff when handling heavy AI workloads without dedicated GPU acceleration. Consequently, this server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, relational databases, memory-cached data stores, software compilation, and intermediate data processing tasks that benefit from its high-capacity local storage and strong integer and vector instruction support.
description: The Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores, 192.0 GB of RAM, and 2835 GB of local storage. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers strong CPU and memory performance, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and Passmark database benchmarks. It achieves high throughput in Redis SET operations and cached memory reads. However, uncached memory bandwidth remains average, and large-scale LLM inference performance is poor due to the lack of GPU acceleration. This server is highly cost-efficient for resource-dense workloads, making it well-suited for database hosting, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
